hook: The monk whose protest split the Church and started the Reformation.

pages.x: Martin Luther was born in Eisleben in 1483, the son of a copper miner who wanted him to be a lawyer. In 1505 a lightning bolt struck near him in a storm, and he cried: "Help me, Saint Anne, and I will become a monk!" Two weeks later, he did.

He prayed, fasted and confessed for hours, but never felt good enough for God. Studying the Bible at Wittenberg, he came to believe that people are saved not by good deeds but by faith alone, as a free gift from God.

The Church was selling indulgences, said to shorten the punishment for sins; one preacher sang: "As soon as the coin in the coffer rings, the soul from purgatory springs." In 1517 Luther wrote 95 arguments against them, and the story says he nailed them to a church door. Printing spread them across Germany in weeks.

In 1521 he was called before the emperor Charles V at the Diet of Worms and ordered to take back his writings. He refused: "Here I stand, I can do no other", as tradition has it. The emperor made him an outlaw whom anyone could kill.

Friends staged a kidnapping and hid him in Wartburg Castle. Disguised as a knight, "Junker Jorg", he translated the New Testament into German in just eleven weeks. His Bible shaped the German language.

In 1525 he married Katharina von Bora, a former nun who had escaped her convent hidden in a wagon among herring barrels. They had six children, and she ran the household, a farm, a brewery and a stream of student lodgers.
Luther started the Protestant Reformation, which split Western Christianity; today hundreds of millions are Protestants. Late in life he also wrote vicious attacks on Jews, later used by the Nazis.
